subject: Firewall approval milestone: private nexus IP permissioning
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: IP permissioning for Private Nexus deployment

Hi Irene / Marissa,

We kicked off the Private Nexus pilot this morning and the infra team asked for a definitive outbound IP set and minimal firewall rules so they can complete the deployment validation in our staging VPC. Can you provide an approved list of control plane egress IPs and any recommended FQDNs/ports for the private endpoint?

Quick context: we'll be running the Redwood Private runtime inside our VPC (on-prem connectivity to the data center via VPN). Our security team needs the list to build a hardened perimeter rule set and to generate evidence for our audit run next week.

What we need from Redwood:
- Single canonical CSV of IPs (IPv4/IPv6 if applicable) for control plane/outbound egress
- Recommended ports and any SNI/FQDN expectations (TLS SNI or SNI-based allowlisting)
- Any short-lived/backstop behaviors (ephemeral NATs, dynamic ranges, fallback endpoints) we should be aware of

Thanks — James

--
James Lee
Cloud Security Lead, Acme Health
james.lee@acmehealth.com
From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: James Lee <james.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IP permissioning for Private Nexus deployment

Hi James — thanks for the context and congrats on getting the pilot running. Attaching a canonical CSV and a short rule template for your firewall team. High level notes below, and I copied David and Kim to confirm the operational bits.

Summary (short):
- Attached: controlplane-egress-ip-list.csv contains the stable control plane egress IPs we use for Private Nexus (columns: region, ip, cidr, purpose). These are the addresses to allow outbound from your private runtime to our control plane.
- Ports: TCP 443 (primary, TLS). We recommend egress-only allow for destination IPs on 443.
- DNS/SNI: We publish a small set of hostnames. If your firewall supports SNI allowlisting (recommended), allow the FQDNs in the firewall-rule-template-v2.xlsx sheet "FQDNs"; otherwise open IPs + 443.
- Ephemeral behavior: We have one fallback region with ephemeral NAT ranges during maintenance windows. The CSV marks these rows with purpose=ephemeral and advises short TTLs on any static mappings.

Operational caveats / ask:
- Please treat the ephemeral rows as 'warmed' fallback — if you want fully static bindings we can export a static-only subset but that reduces failover flexibility.
- If the team needs a signed attest of the list for audit, we can provide a signed PDF and rotation schedule.

Attaching: controlplane-egress-ip-list.csv (CSV, 2 KB), firewall-rule-template-v2.xlsx (Excel, 85 KB), private-nexus-network-diagram.png (PNG, 420 KB).

If this looks good, Marissa/David — can you ack and confirm whether the fallback ephemeral rows are acceptable for Acme or whether they want a static-only export?

Thanks,
Irene
--
Irene Choi
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Date: 2027-10-18T15:28:00-07:00

On Mon, Oct 18, 2027 at 11:05 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi James — thanks for the context and congrats on getting the pilot running. Attaching a canonical CSV and a short rule template for your firewall team. High level notes below, and I copied David and Kim to confirm the operational bits.
> 
> Summary (short):
> - Attached: controlplane-egress-ip-list.csv contains the stable control plane egress IPs we use for Private Nexus (columns: region, ip, cidr, purpose). These are the addresses to allow outbound from your private runtime to our control plane.

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side before we lock rules: 
1) Can you confirm whether the CSV contains both IPv4 and IPv6? We currently aim to block all IPv6 outbound unless explicitly required.
2) For the ephemeral rows: what's the expected frequency of rotation (daily/weekly/monthly)? We need to document rotation frequency in our config management.

Also — we prefer deny-by-default and only allow specific FQDN/SNI entries. If Redwood can publish stable TLS A records or a stable public CN for the control plane that would let us avoid IP-level whitelisting entirely. Is that an option?

Thanks,
Maya Rao
On-prem Security Operations, Acme Health
ops-security@acmehealth.com
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Maya Rao <ops-security@acmehealth.com>, James Lee <james.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-19T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IP permissioning for Private Nexus deployment

Hi Maya / James — following up with answers and the export you requested.

1) IPv6: The current Private Nexus control plane endpoints are IPv4-only today. The CSV contains IPv4 rows only and we flagged IPv6=false in the CSV metadata. If you require IPv6 in future, please flag in this thread and we'll prioritize an IPv6 CIDR export.

2) Ephemeral rotation cadence: fallback/ephemeral NAT ranges rotate weekly by default; stable control plane IPs rotate on a quarterly schedule for planned maintenance events. We document rotations in our published status page and will provide a monthly rotation digest if you need it for CM.

3) SNI/FQDN option: Yes — we can provide stable FQDNs for the control plane TLS endpoints (listed in the attached Excel, sheet "FQDNs") and we recommend SNI allowlisting where possible. That is the preferred approach for deny-by-default per your policy. We will provide a short, signed attestation PDF and a rotation SLA (30 days notice for planned changes) after you confirm SNI acceptance.

Next steps:
- I've exported a "static-only" CSV subset as controlplane-egress-ip-list-static-only.csv and uploaded it to the Drive folder (link above) for your change control team. Use that if you cannot tolerate weekly rotation.
- If ok, please confirm in this thread which set you'll import (static-only vs full including ephemeral) and whether you'll adopt SNI/FQDN allowlisting.

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Onboarding, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
